authority.source_authority: Logos retains Scripture-domain and local governance authority; DAD receives metadata only after an explicit later gate.

non_overlap_statement: The integration foreman owns the final write set; bounded specialists may write only their assigned non-overlapping component paths, and the independent checker is read-only.

roles.why_needed: The family spans authority, contracts, catalogs, routing, tests, and release gates that require one accountable integrator.
roles.mission: Integrate the additive candidate family without changing chunk output, gold, canon, graph truth, preferred readings, or theology authority.
inputs: existing Logos chunking governance and registries
roles.authority: May write only the T500 allowed paths and must stop at every owner-gated promotion or DAD-publication boundary.
acceptance_conditions: All constituent contracts and validators pass.
No forbidden output or authority surface changes.
stop_conditions: A change requires new Scripture, canon, theology, chunk-output, gold, or DAD execution authority.

readiness_conditions: Specialist component checks pass and the final diff is bounded.

roles.why_needed: The constitution, role packs, aliases, and routing policy require focused domain-governance modeling.
roles.mission: Implement family configuration and compatibility contracts under the existing owner-authorized Scripture-first principle.
roles.authority: May write only config/agents/families/scripture-first-biblical-chunking and the bounded compatibility-alias section in config/agents/agent_roles.yaml.
acceptance_conditions: All requested control roles and specialist packs are represented.
stop_conditions: The work would duplicate source authority or alter an existing chunking skill lifecycle.

readiness_conditions: YAML parses and no unrelated role definitions change.

roles.why_needed: Four versioned contracts and fail-closed negative cases require a separate contract-focused implementation lane.
roles.mission: Implement the four JSON Schemas and representative positive and negative fixtures without defining domain authority beyond T500.
roles.authority: May write only the four T500 schema files and tests/fixtures/scripture_first_biblical_chunking_family.
acceptance_conditions: Schemas express identity separation, canonical-66 scope, specialist limits, evidence lanes, and hold behavior.
Negative fixtures fail for the intended reason.
stop_conditions: A schema would authorize output promotion or embed Scripture/source payloads.

readiness_conditions: Files parse as JSON and references are local and resolvable.

roles.why_needed: A distinct reviewer must challenge theological imputation, self-approval, authority leakage, and regression risk.
roles.mission: Independently verify the completed family, evidence precedence, hold behavior, route isolation, privacy boundary, and non-output-changing status.
roles.authority: Read-only review; cannot edit, approve its own work, activate candidates, promote gold, or publish to DAD.
acceptance_conditions: Independent findings name evidence and severity.
Release gate is explicit and preserves owner decisions.
stop_conditions: Checker identity collides with a writer or required raw evidence is unavailable.

readiness_conditions: Integration is frozen for review and all permitted evidence is available.

proof_obligations.description: Prove T500 adds only candidate control-plane artifacts and changes no chunk, gold, canon, graph, retrieval, preferred-reading, or theology truth.
Prove prohibited first-pass evidence, unresolved authority references, writer/checker collisions, and over-delegation fail closed.
Prove any DAD adaptation remains gated and can contain hashes and capability metadata but no Scripture or private source payloads.

unresolved_decisions.summary: DAD publication remains deferred until its candidate family framework is merged and portfolio registry/documentation drift is reconciled.
Before pilots, orchestration must resolve each parent assignment packet and verify lane equality across the packet collection.
Any activation or replacement of the incumbent requires Lowell's explicit approval in a separate task.
